compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
T5c (the security overlay, exec AGENT) reviews plans under the gate-wide reviewing stance in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:264-274` (`_SHARED_PREAMBLE`), whose line "Evaluate the spec AS WRITTEN, not the current codebase" (passes.py:269) is prepended to EVERY plan-review pass prompt by `_resolve_system` (passes.py:276-292). The T5c rubric file itself (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md`) contains NO as-written text — the stance arrives via the shared preamble. For a security criterion that stance is out of step with surveyed LLM security-review tools (exploitability is a property of the system, not of the text): 46% of T5c's strong findings already cite repo artifacts despite it. Separately, 30% of T5c advisories are pure "does not declare X" template shape that Pass-2 cannot drop (the statement is literally true, so it verifies); 99 reviews carried >= 2 same-shape findings; and T5c advisories displaced other criteria in 103 advisory-cap-limited reviews. The existing SAME-ROUND DEDUP rule in the rubric body (plan_review_T5c.md line 19) dedupes per (surface, defect) PAIR, so a plan with N undeclared surfaces still yields N findings — the new rule is strictly tighter for this one template class. The operator approved: the grounded rewrite, blocking at 0.90, and dedup-at-source plus severity demotion instead of hard citation suppression.

Prior art / supersession: ticket d156-7eb5-b4f0-40c3 (closed) hardened this same rubric explicitly "without changing its posture (advisory @ 0.95)"; this story is the operator-approved follow-on that DOES change the posture — it deliberately supersedes that earlier constraint. Ticket 9374 (S7) is concurrently relocating `_SHARED_PREAMBLE` into prompts.py, so this story must NOT edit passes.py or prompts.py: the grounding change is a criterion-LOCAL override inside the T5c rubric only, which stays correct wherever the preamble lives.

## Approach
All three behavior changes are rubric text — instructions to the Pass-1 finder — following the T10 precedent bfa8 (commit e3962d21e) just landed: "severity guidance, not new machinery". The only non-test config change is two fields in the T5c routing entry. No changes to pass3_decide, orchestrator.py, passes.py, prompts.py, or det_gate_rules.py.

1. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md` — four rubric-body edits, preserving every phrase pinned by tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:502-543 (trust-boundary gate first, loopback/not-applicable carve-out, mixed-scope rule, zero-trust caveat, T10 "no blurring" scope note):
   - GROUNDING OVERRIDE sentence: "GROUNDING OVERRIDE (this criterion only): unlike the shared reviewing stance's evaluate-the-spec-AS-WRITTEN default, ground the plan's security implications in the CURRENT codebase and configuration via the read tools — a control defined elsewhere (existing auth middleware, an existing config guard, an ignore rule) FLIPS a finding; verify before you flag." This works as a criterion-local override because the rubric is rendered into the SAME request as the preamble (`_resolve_system` compiles rubric + preamble together, passes.py:276-292) and the criterion-specific instruction is the more specific directive.
   - DEDUP-AT-SOURCE (tightens the existing SAME-ROUND DEDUP sentence for the one template class): emit at most ONE undeclared-access-posture finding per plan; when several surfaces lack a declared access posture, fold the additional surfaces into that single finding's evidence rather than emitting one finding per surface.
   - DEMOTION, not suppression (extends the existing "SEVERITY priors ... these bias how hard you press" sentence in its own idiom): a candidate finding that cites neither a repo artifact you actually read with the tools nor a quoted plan sentence must be pressed at MINOR — demoted, never suppressed (the grounded 46% keep their strength; the ungrounded lose blocking reach).
   - HIGH-class scoping sentence (structural mirror of T10's bfa8 sentence): "ONLY these two HIGH classes warrant severity >= major — a plaintext secret on a boundary-crossing path; an undeclared internet-reachable sensitive surface; every other finding is at most minor." This is consistent with the rubric's existing SEVERITY priors line, which already names exactly these two shapes as HIGH.
   Mechanism (why rubric text is the right lever): the Pass-1 finder emits NO severity field (passes.py:7 — `{finding, criteria[], evidence[], scenarios[], impact}` — severity/priority are computed deterministically in Pass 3 from Pass-2 graded attributes); rubric severity language shapes how the finder frames and presses evidence, which is exactly how bfa8 scoped T10's 0.90 blocking to its four MAJOR classes with zero pass3_decide changes — "so lesser findings cannot reach the 0.90 bar through the existing severity->priority pipeline". Blocking itself stays criterion-wide (there is NO per-class blocking mechanism in Pass-3, and this plan does not invent one); the HIGH-class sentence is what keeps non-HIGH findings below the bar.
2. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` T5c entry (lines 385-386): `"block_threshold": 0.95 -> 0.9` and `"default_posture": "advisory" -> "blocking"`. These are the plan-review gate's ONLY blocking controls: `threshold_for` (src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:45-81) blocks for gate="plan_review" iff `default_posture == "blocking"`. The `blocking_enabled` field is the code-review gate's convention, INERT for plan-review, and is NOT added (convention pinned by tests/unit/test_project_symbol_reference_completeness.py::test_routing_entry_carries_no_inert_blocking_enabled_key). The checklist array in the entry is unchanged.
3. Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` via `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` (the command the guide's own header names; registry.py:604).

Execution stays AGENT; NO DET keyword gate for T5c — the audit showed the best candidate gate fires on 66% of plans while missing real findings (security findings live in plans without security words), unlike T10's 28%/100% rule. Alternative rejected: 1-TURN demotion of the whole criterion — forfeits the repo grounding that produces T5c's best findings. Rollback: a one-commit git revert of the two routing lines restores advisory @ 0.95 (rubric text can stay; it is strictly FP-reducing) — no data or schema migration. The blocking path reuses the existing pass3 machinery end-to-end, so no new failure modes or fail-open/fail-closed policy are introduced; block events land in the signed REVIEW_RESULT sidecars, and post-land behavioral outcomes (grounding rate, template-shape rate) are monitored by the same zero-LLM criterion-effectiveness recorder the bfa8 pilot uses — unit tests pin rubric text and Pass-3 mechanics, deliberately not LLM behavior.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md — rubric rewrite (four sentences).
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json — T5c posture/threshold only.
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py — extend the three `["T3", "T10"]` parametrizations (lines 91, 102, 111) with "T5c".
- tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py — EXPECTED_ROUTING line 68 `"T5c": (0.95, "advisory") -> (0.9, "blocking")`; add T5c to the pilot-blocking set consumed by test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking (lines 152-158).
- tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py — add "T5c" to _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING (line 111).
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_t5c_grounding.py — NEW rubric-text pin module (tests/llm/ does not exist; tests/unit/plan_review/ is the home of the analogous bfa8 tests).
- docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md — regenerated output.
Out of scope: passes.py / prompts.py (ticket 9374 owns the preamble), orchestrator.py, review_kernel/decide.py, det_gate_rules.py.

## Testing
All tests under tests/unit/ (there is no tests/llm/ directory). Exact AC-to-test mapping:
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py (extended parametrizations): the T5c routing entry carries default_posture "blocking" @ 0.9 and `threshold_for(["T5c"], ..., gate="plan_review")` resolves (0.9, True); a T5c finding pinned at priority 0.92 gets decision "block" and one at 0.85 stays "advisory" through the REAL `pass3_over_findings` wrapper (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:737) — covers AC3.
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_t5c_grounding.py (new; same pattern as that file's test_t10_rubric_contains_major_class_severity_guidance — read the .md, assert exact phrases): (a) the grounding-override sentence (read tools + current codebase + a-control-defined-elsewhere-flips-a-finding), (b) the one-undeclared-access-posture-finding-per-plan cap, (c) the ungrounded-pressed-at-minor demotion wording ("demoted, never suppressed"), (d) the two-HIGH-class severity sentence with both class phrases — covers AC1/AC2.
- Updated pins: test_threshold_recalibration.py (full pinned routing table + exact blocking set) and test_impact_model_versioning.py (approved plan-review blocking set) — all THREE pinned blocking-set assertions gain T5c in the same commit, so no pin is left contradicting the routing change.
- Regression: tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_t5c_leads_with_trust_boundary_scope_gate and ::test_t10_not_reframed_by_trust_boundary_generalisation pass UNMODIFIED (the rewrite preserves the pinned trust-boundary body phrases).
- Guide currency oracle: after the commit, re-running `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` leaves `git diff -- docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` empty.
- Gates: `make lint && make typecheck`, targeted pytest on the four test modules, then the full `pytest tests/unit`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] plan_review_T5c.md carries the criterion-local GROUNDING OVERRIDE (tool-grounded evaluation against the current codebase/configuration; a control defined elsewhere flips a finding) and the two-HIGH-class severity-scoping sentence, with all previously pinned trust-boundary phrases intact (checked: tests/unit/plan_review/test_t5c_grounding.py string assertions + existing test_plan_review.py T5c pins green unmodified).
- [ ] The rubric caps undeclared-access-posture findings at ONE per plan (extra surfaces folded into that finding's evidence) and demotes candidate findings citing neither a read repo artifact nor a quoted plan sentence to minor — demoted, not suppressed (checked: test_t5c_grounding.py string assertions).
- [ ] criteria_routing.json T5c has default_posture "blocking", block_threshold 0.9, and NO blocking_enabled key; a T5c finding at priority 0.92 blocks and at 0.85 stays advisory through pass3_over_findings (checked: extended test_criteria_blocking.py parametrizations).
- [ ] All three pinned blocking-set assertions (test_threshold_recalibration.py EXPECTED_ROUTING + blocking-set test, test_impact_model_versioning.py approved set) include T5c and the full tests/unit suite is green (checked: CI Verified gate).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md is regenerated and current (checked: re-running the regenerate-criteria-guide command yields an empty git diff for the guide).
